english.title: Provider etc of goods / services etc require supply / production of record of data subjects access - Data Protection
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person concerned with the provision (for payment or not) of goods, facilities or services to the public, or a section of the public, as a condition of

(A)_[providing goods, facilities or services to **(..SPECIFY NAME..)]_
(B)_[offering to provide goods, facilities or services to **(..SPECIFY NAME..)]_

required

(C)_[that person]_
(D)_[a third party, namely **(..SPECIFY..)]_

(E)_[to supply you with]_
(F)_[to produce to you]_

a relevant record obtained under the data subject's right of access provisions
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 56(2), 56(5) and 60(2) of the Data Protection Act 1998.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Prosecution only by Commissioner or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions
(ii) See Part IV of the Act for exemptions
(iii) See section 55(3) for exceptions
(iv) See section 56(6), (7), (8), (9) and (10) for definitions

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

INDICTMENT: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
